newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) on Friday will be broadcast live on state television and on the Internet.
Finance Minister P.Chidambaram is scheduled to unveil
his budget proposals in a speech to parliament at 5.00 p.m. (1130 GMT).
** India said on Thursday there was a significant fall in its external debt but added it needed to do more to reduce its indebtedness which continued to be a matter of concern.
The stock of external debt declined to $92.20 billion at
the end of 1995/96 (April-March) from $99.01 billion one year earlier, the government said in a status report on external debt presented to parliament.

** Indian industry, grappling with high interest rates and flagging output growth, expects the government to remove some painful corporate taxes in the federal budget, top business leaders said on Thursday.
They said the 1997/98 budget for the fiscal year
starting on April 1 would need to remove a controversial tax on profits and a surcharge on corporate tax to revive languid capital markets and spur industrial growth.

** India's centre-left ruling coalition could widen the scope of a federal expenditure tax to cover luxury items like cars and high-end consumer durables in its annual budget, analysts said on Thursday.
** An overvalued rupee is contributing to a slowdown in Indian exports, representatives of the country's export industries said on Thursday.
MARKETS:
** Blue chips at major Indian bourses rallied in hectic trade on Thursday on market optimism ahead of Friday's budget, dealers said.
** The Bombay Stock Exchange's 30-share index jumped 62.90 points, or 1.87 percent, to 3,427.87.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index climbed up 23.90 points, or 2.4 percent, to 992.75.
** The Delhi share index .DE rose 16.15 points to 744.41.
** The Calcutta share index gained 5.74 points to 448.45.
** The Madras share index climbed 50.60 points to 3,393.80.
